\caption{PQC overhead of the serial schedule: the inputs of the distance results in Table~\ref{tab:dmax_results}. $T_{\mathrm{KEM}}$ is one encapsulation plus one decapsulation (key generation amortized over the reusable key) from public single-core cycle counts normalized to a $3$~GHz clock, fast and portable denoting the AVX2 and portable C implementations of Kyber512/768/1024 (standardized as ML-KEM-512/768/1024~\cite{FIPS203}) and the AES-NI and plain-C SHAKE variants of FrodoKEM~\cite{KyberSpec2021,FrodoKEMSpec2021}. $|C_1|$ is the ciphertext size of the cited specifications; $T_{\mathrm{ser}}$ serializes $C_1$ plus the $29$-byte AEAD message $C_2$ at an assumed $1$~Gb/s; $T_{\text{fixed}}$ is the resulting distance-independent delay (Methods); Cat.\ is the NIST security category. The no-PQC row, which sends the two correction bits as one plaintext byte, is a latency lower-bound reference that offers no equivalent protection. These are microbenchmarks of the classical primitives, not end-to-end teleportation measurements; benchmark sources, variant identities and the values measured on the authors' hardware are documented in Supplementary Note~\SIref{si:jedi}.}
